Chapter Six, part one

I smacked my lips together immediately after I woke up the next afternoon and it tasted like a cat took a shit in my mouth. Speaking of fecal metaphors, I felt like five pounds of dog shit in a two-pound bag. I opened my eyes for the glaring sun to greet me with a searing pain on both of my temples. I got up and went to take a leak. I come out to hear the Guns N’ Roses rendition of “Live and Let Die” blaring from my TV. I had left it on all night and let the website I was on cycle through my favorite music videos.

I had two choices. One, I could head back to the couch and go back to sleep. This would also require me to walk to my bedroom to grab a blanket and a few pillows--one for my head and another to block out that godawful fucking light. This option required too much effort. Option two was to attempt hair of the dog again--this wasn’t happening. I make a detour towards the kitchen. I grab the glass that I had drank out of the night before, rinsed it out in my sink, and drank the tallest glass of water I could ever imagine. I eyeballed all of the scattered, empty or half-empty cans littering the table--or at least the general vicinity of my table--and the lone bottle sitting sideways next to the door. Picking up after myself and being a responsible fucking adult was well out of the question at this night. I drink another glass of water.

I had dreams about that moment the night before. After a long night of aggressive drinking, I have the “thirst dreams” where I would be thirsty and drink cup after cup of water without it quenching me. Those were often the worst nights. I pop about three, maybe four Aspirin and throw a whole bunch of frozen vegetables and yogurt into a blender. I love my drunk idiot logic; somehow a whole bunch of healthy stuff will counteract the poison that I willingly ingested into my body the night before. If somehow that worked, I would be richest man alive--as if I were to be the first one to discover such a remedy.

So after it was apparent that replenishing my electrolytes and putting some food into my stomach wasn’t going to be a work, I brought out the heavy duty shit: pickle juice. If there is one go-to hangover remedy. It is chalked full of salts and other electrolytes to replace what you pissed out the night before. It also has a lot of vinegar and spices to wash out your system of any remaining toxins. At least it works for me in a pinch.

As I slurp down my concoction and chug my pickle juice. I gather my recollections from last night. Did I really kick Brandon out of my apartment. What for? Oh yeah, what a dickhead. He had to been telling the truth. I don’t remember very much about the way it went down, though. Vodka has the tendency to make things blur together. A toddler’s finger-painting masterpiece was better organized than my memory of last night. I really shouldn’t feel bad for the guy, but I did. I kind of went off on him. He was toasted and I made him drive home. I walk up to my laptop, which was still open and plugged in from the night before, and found out that I was still recording. I got his confession on video--the poor bastard.

Part two

“You know what?”, the cynic in the back of my mind exclaimed, “fuck that motherfucker. “Yeah, but what if something bad happened to him or he got someone else killed? Then what?”, my more anxious and worrisome side intervened. Finally, rationality kicked in, “the chances of that shit happening are pretty slim. He probably made it home okay. Quit being such a goddamn drama queen. He fooled around with your ex. She is a skank. He is a dickhead. You shouldn’t have any concern for him besides his personal safety, at least not right this second.

After eating, or rather drinking, the breakfast of champions, I lay back down and watch more music videos on my couch while curled up in a blanket like a sick child. I drifted off to sleep for another several hours and woke up still feeling like a piece of shit. This time, I felt like a different piece of shit--a more recuperated and better focused piece of shit. I glanced at my clock and cursed the fact that it was almost five o’clock in the evening. It was Saturday night and I had to do something with myself. I peeled my ass off my couch and spent a solid twenty minutes sulking in the shower, lamenting the state of my body and my liver. Whoever tells you that they don’t get hangovers is a bullshit liar.

I get out and throw on a pair of shorts. En route, I head back to the kitchen for some more pickle juice. With the ferocity and frequency that I drink nowadays, I thought it would be best to buy the giant plastic jars in bulk. As I left the kitchen, the couch calls my name and asks me politely to sit back down. I found it strangely persuasive as I curl back up and fall asleep until around 8:30. It’s not like after a night like the one before that I would have done anything productive. I’m a useless bag of smashed assholes after a night dedicated to drinking cheap-ass hard alcohol.

Part three

This hangover needed to go away, so I stepped it up a notch. I slammed down another two glasses of pickle juice and threw more fruit in the blender. This time, as I collected up the cans to throw in the trash bin, I picked up the bottle and poured the remaining contents into the blender. If I was going to go off and do something with my night, goddammit, I was going to do it right.

After I threw on some clothes that were conveniently enough for the first time in ages hung in my closet, I drove to the local bar a few blocks away from my house. I lived off of 71st and Wornall, so there is pretty much nothing to do at this time on a Saturday night except drink. There are lots of places in Waldo to choose from: places that are well-lit, dark places, nice places, shady places, places that are ridiculously loud, quiet places spare the chatter of conversations, places with rough crowds, and places with decent people.

The place that I frequent is a small shack that is a little bit off of the beaten path near 75th and Wornall that is littered with bars and restaurants. I like it because very few people actually know about this, and consequently, cannot shit it up. I know the regulars and hardly anybody new walks in. I order a beer and nurse on it while i putz around on my phone. One of the regulars strikes up a conversation with me about the bowling game in the corner. I drown out his words and nod in agreement every so often. My attention is geared towards the fact that the top ten list on the bowling game; seven out of the nine entries are “ASS”. This was definitely my kind of place.

After a drink or two, my buddy Rick walked in through the door. Depending on his mood and relative level of abbreviation, he could become P-Rick at any time. He grabs the barstool next to me and sits down.

“What’s up, Vince? I haven’t seen you in a while.”, he said.

There is a reason for that.

“Dude, you know I nailed Carly the other night, right?”

“No, when was this?”, I said. No, I didn’t know and, no, I don’t care.

“It was last Saturday in the parking lot behind Dingo’s. Me and her friend were hanging out, we go to leave, we get busy, and then I picked her up and put her right on top of me in the passenger's seat”.

I doubt that’s what he said in reality. He uses a much less sophisticated system of grunts and hand gestures followed by a dumb chuckle to get his point across.

Part four

And as if I wanted to hear more--”And then she invited me back to her place where we had a three-way”, he said. Good for you, but I still don’t care.

“Her friend was sucking my dick while Carly sat on my face. Then she rode me until we came all of the place.” Congratulations, man. You found sluts. You should get checked out.

Right before I could comment on his “accomplishment”, the bartender walked by and I asked for a shot and a drink.

“What do you want a shot of?”

I asked for a Thunder and Lightning:

-4oz 151 proof rum, any brand
-40z of 100 proof peppermint schnapps 
-Serve chilled in a shotglass

If this didn’t help me drown out P-Rick’s bullshit, I was going to lose my shit. You would think that showing active disinterest would be enough to dissuade someone from telling the rest of their shitty ass story. He was still sitting across from me making hand gestures over his lap like he was sitting someone down with the most stupid, toothy grin I have ever seen on his long face.

Over across the way I saw a woman in a leopard skin tank top and yoga pants drinking a Long Island Ice Tea. I nudge Rick on the shoulder.

“Hey, what do you think about that girl over there?”, I said.

“I don’t know. Let’s take shots and find out”. Great--he’s fucking with me.

I order another Thunder and Lightning. He wanted the same thing, but I hinted to the bartender, Stu, that his drink should be a little less, say, potent. There have been times in the past where he would come in, get beyond shithoused, and cause trouble. Stu has had to bar him at least twice for only god knows what. It’s a miracle that he is still allowed in here. I catch a glimpse of Stu behind the bar mixing in some water with a lower proof schnapps. He walks right over to place our shots down on the bar, first mine followed by his shot.

“Here’s to pussy”, he said.

“Yeah, that.” We touch glasses and slam them down to the top of the bar before shooting. Stu has been watering down his drinks for months and I’m surprised he hasn’t noticed yet. Our hapless bartender is a quiet man who has a penchant for one-liners and seeing how far he can push a prank until it gets out of control.

“So, now, what about the girl at the far end of the bar in the yoga pants?”, I said.

“Yeah, man. I don’t know. Those aren’t yoga pants, that’s spandex.

“I think you’re full of shit.”

“You like fat chicks, why don’t you have at it?”

“Dude, not every woman who doesn’t look like a pretty petite 15 year-old girl is fat.”

“No, dude. She’s fat.”

Part five

“You’re just mad because any woman that is heavier than 110 pounds soaking wet could break your scrawny ass in half.” This was a true story. He was about 5’ 11” and was thin as a rail. As much as he brags about going to the gym all the time, he has no gains to show for it.

“Dude, I’m telling you. She’s fat.”

“She’s not. You just think she’s out of your league.”, I said.

“No, man, that’s not what I’m saying at all.”

“Then why don’t you go over there and take a shot?”

“Because I don’t want to”.

“Fine, I will.” I had about enough of his shit anyways. I get up, stand next to her, and order a shot.

“What’s in a Thunder and Lightning?’, she said.

Honestly, she did not look that bad. She looked a bit, let’s say, chunky, but can you really blame a girl for that? It’s not a one-size-fits-all-fashion-model-size-zero world. People just happen to come in all shapes and sizes. At any rate, I turn to her and tell her exactly what’s in it. It’s not like it’s the first time since coming to this bar that a woman has asked me that question.

“Oh, wow. You’ve got balls.”, she said.

“It’s really not that bad. You just have to be careful because it will put you on your ass.”

“I bet. My name is Victoria.”

We exchange greetings and eventually she buys a shot so she can take one with me. On the count of taking three of these ass-kickingly powerful shots in the past twenty minutes, my hangover was history, and less fortunately, things begin to mesh together. I was still very aware of what I was doing. My motor skills were still there, but this was very much unlike the vodka drunk where I was in absolute control of my surroundings. The only difference was that I simply didn’t remember a whole lot from the next hour or so. I remember asking for a glass of pickle juice. I remember bragging about how effective pickle juice was in curing hangovers and how it makes me somewhat functional when I need to be. I remember her telling me that she was an activities planner for a non-profit organization and that she wanted to dye her hair purple.

After two glasses of pickle juice and switching to beer for the time being, I began to recollect some of my memories.

Part six

“...and we were picketing, one thousand strong, sending out our message about rape culture in the West and how the patriarchy was denying it. We had people give us some weird glances and even some cat calls. Fuck them because no means no, dammit!”, she said.

“Very intriguing.” I slammed down the next two pints that came my way and went right back into a state of blissful ignorance for at least the next forty five minutes. At least I think it was forty five minutes; maybe it was fifteen minutes.

“You know, I really appreciate you listening to me. This shit is important and everybody wants to put me down for supporting this stuff. Do you want to come back to my place and talk about it some more?”

“Yeah...sure.”

The funny thing that I learned about myself is that no matter how wasted I get at a bar, I have never, ever forgotten to pay a tab. I do this as soon as I could and we took her car back to her place. I don’t remember a whole lot about the drive except we went north a little bit. No, never mind. I at least recalled that we ended up somewhere in Brookside, roughly twenty blocks away from my place. I remember getting out of the car and needing to use the bathroom.

Part seven

I stood over the toilet and felt a grumble in my stomach. Fuck me running; this cannot be happening now. The great thing about pickle juice as a remedy is that it flushes out your system, and I mean everything. You know what? I’m going to put it this way--I needed to fart...and so I did. I felt immediate relief and, for a second, believed I was in the clear before I felt something drip down my leg.

And so I stand in the bathroom of a perfect stranger’s house who is willing to sleep with me, mind you, and my worst fears have come true. I am totally repulsed by bathroom stuff. Anything about farting or pooping is absolutely repugnant to me. As luck would have it, this could not have happened at a worse time. I could feel the heat on my face from the glowing. I peered at myself in the mirror and thought “Look at you, you disgusting fuck. You just shit your pants. Way to be a fucking adult.” I heard steps in the hallway and realized that I didn’t have any time to beat myself up over this too much longer. I dove straight for the toilet paper to, you know, clean myself off. This worked only to some extent.

I needed a way to hide the evidence. As I recalled, there was a storm drain right outside on the edge of the street right in front of her house. I jumped straight out for the bathroom, ran through the living room, bolted out the door, and ran for the drain. At last, I could see it, the edge of the drain, I was almost home free. About mid-toss, I heard a voice booming behind me.

“Where are you going?”

“Oh, nowhere. I was just making a phone call. It was supposed to, um, be an emergency, but, you know, it’s not.” I look back over to the edge of the street and found that my toss was only half successful. My underwear laid on the very edge of the gutter for the whole world to see. Will they know it was me? I doubt it. I headed back inside to find her laying under the sheets in a dark room lit by a single candle.

Part eight

I was woken up the next morning by the light breaking through her shades. I felt her shuffle around a little bit in bed when I rolled over to put my arms around her.

“What the actual fuck”, I said to myself after opening my eyes. P-Rick was right; she was a biggun.

You know, you have to hand it to the service industry and their ingenuity. The dangerous mix of hard liquor and bar lighting has done more to mask imperfections than anything else in the history of anything, ever. Last night it fooled the everloving fuck out of me.

I spent the next fifteen minutes trying to pry my arm free of her so I could recover my clothes and walk the twenty blocks back to the bar. I found my shirt and my socks wrapped up in the comforter. Fortunately, my pants and shoes were on the floor. That leaves one remaining question: where the fuck were my underwear?

I had no time for this shit. I threw my clothes on as fast as humanly possible and tip-toed towards the door. Once I gently shut the door and completed my escape attempt, I walk out onto the street and found my underwear still hanging on the edge of the gutter.

“Oh yeah”, I said. I never said I was the brightest bulb in the box. I check my pockets to make sure I didn’t leave anything behind. I sighed heavily when I found out that everything was accounted for. I pulled out my phone and dialed up Rick.

“Dude, you’re not going to believe what happened”.
